content.text: {"answer":"None of the supplied papers directly addresses “graph machine learning for chemical reactions.” They all focus on text/linguistic analysis, authorship/style measurement, or general effects of LLMs on writing style, not on chemical reaction graphs or reaction modeling. For example, several papers study authorship verification and stylistic drift in text under AI-assisted writing or distribution shifts [2,4,6,9,10], while others analyze how LLM rewriting or post-editing changes style similarity and linguistic markers [1,3,5,8]. Another paper builds an authorship stylometry approach using language models [7].\n\nIf you meant “graph” in the sense of analyzing relationships (e.g., an academic genealogy graph), paper [6] uses a mathematics genealogy graph of advisor–student links to study stylistic similarity. However, it is about author writing style, not chemical reaction learning.","grounded":false}

validation_error: Grounded answers must cite papers; ungrounded answers must not
